source.title: From promise to practice: realizing high-performance decentralized training
source.authors: Ze-Sen Wang; Jiao-Jiao Zhang; Xu-Yang Wu; Mikael Johansson

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no garbling or cutoff apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out generalization results for decentralized training on translation, image classification, and GPT-2 pretraining, settings not covered by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports generalization metrics for decentralized Adam variants against All-Reduce Adam, but does not test random-label memorization, widening, convolutional versus fully connected models, adaptive versus SGD optimizers, large versus small batches, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Table 1 and runtime results are not rows because they measure communication or runtime rather than generalization.
record.test_reason: The study compares decentralized Adam variants with All-Reduce Adam-based training at fixed global batch sizes. None of its results tests V1–V8. It cites the large-batch generalization penalty to justify keeping global batch sizes fixed; a new setting with held-out metrics alone does not qualify as T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: their decentralized implementation trains faster than standard All-Reduce without compromising generalization in the tested practical settings. Their stronger statement that AccumAdam always outperforms the alternatives is not uniformly borne out by every translation metric and topology.
record.recipe_differences: Compares decentralized Adam and accumulated Adam with All-Reduce Adam; the interventions concern decentralized communication and optimizer updates, not the versions' original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Translation scores vary across method and communication topology; the paper reports different results for Complete and AER topologies. ImageNet results also vary by decentralized method and topology.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed global batch sizes and training budgets, decentralized Adam variants yield competitive held-out performance. AccumAdam improves ImageNet top-1 accuracy to 76.34–76.54 versus 76.01 for All-Reduce; DAdam reaches 75.27–75.31. AccumAdam also lowers GPT-2 validation loss from 2.8626 to 2.8561. Translation results vary with method, topology, and metric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decentralized Adam-based training can achieve competitive or improved held-out performance relative to All-Reduce Adam-based training under selected fixed-budget recipes.

record.code_released: The code will be open source upon acceptance.
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty for the ImageNet table or GPT-2 comparison. Its experiments compare decentralized and All-Reduce variants, not the claim-version interventions; GPT-2 reports losses rather than a direct generalization-gap measure.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible generalization results were omitted. Runtime and communication measurements, including Table 1 and Section 5.2 runtime comparisons, do not measure the claim's generalization behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, including tuning and recovery interventions.
Large versus small global batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations; global batch sizes are held fixed here.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No eligible V1–V8 results are missing. Table 4's additional eight-worker comparisons and Table 2's omitted DAdam AER English–French result also fit no version. The supplied manuscript is under review; it does not establish the record's claimed peer-reviewed status. Training algorithms are incorrectly typed as models throughout the record.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under natural labels are not compared.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or dropout ablation comparison.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relation.reason: Section 1.1 and Appendix A.6 cite large-batch generalization findings, but the study neither tests a listed version nor uses its effect as a method.

tranche.reason: The experiments compare decentralized Adam variants with All-Reduce Adam-based training at fixed global batch sizes. They test none of V1–V8; the large-batch penalty is cited as motivation for experimental controls.

source_check.notes: All 16 rows describe the study's method performance and should remain background rather than claim-evidence rows; runtime should be separated from generalization metrics. The authors' conclusion is accurately represented, but their blanket AccumAdam-superiority statement does not hold for every translation metric and topology.
